newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge plans to raise stake in Dutch unit.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge plans to raise stake in Dutch unit.

text.p: Major Belgian insurer Royale Belge said on Wednesday it was planning to raise its 51-percent stake in Dutch Groep UAP-NieuwRotterdam.

"We certainly want to develop our core business. We have 51 percent in UAP-NieuwRotterdam and our vocation in the longer term is to go beyond that," managing director Jean-Pierre Gerard told a news briefing.
UAP-NieuwRotterdam fully controls Dutch insurers UAP Nederland and Nieuw Rotterdam Beheer, which legally merged in July and are eighth largest in the Netherlands with a market share of 4.2 percent.
Gerard said French Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) -- which holds a 49 percent direct and indirect stake in Royale Belge -- had a 43 percent stake in UAP-NieuwRotterdam.

He did not say how much Royale Belge would have to pay for the remaining 49 percent but that the "yield of the sale of its Tractebel shares more or less corresponded with the amount which had to be invested to purchase UAP's stake (in UAP-NieuwRotterdam)".

Royale Belge said on Tuesday it would book a four billion franc capital gain from the sale of its stake in energy and engineering holding company Tractebel to Belgian holding Societe Generale de Belgique. It said the transaction would bring in a total of 8.2 billion.
"It (raising the stake in UAP-Nieuw-Rotterdam) is certainly one of the possibilities that will be raised with shareholders in the next few months," Gerard said.
He added most of Royale Belge's Dutch operations were being centralised in Utrecht, southern Netherlands.
He said the merger of operations of the two insurers allowed Royale Belge to cut operating costs and improve earnings.
"The Dutch insurance companies should be able to contribute to a larger extent to the consolidated result in the upcoming years," Royale Belge said in a statement.
